_comment: The `meshweaver` ACR retention tasks, as they exist in Azure. Read back with
`az acr task show`, 2026-09-07 (MeshWeaver#3438).
🚨 THESE TASKS ARE CLOUD-ONLY. `az acr task show` returns an `EncodedTask` with
`contextPath: null` — the YAML is stored base64-encoded inside Azure with no source
repository — and an org-wide code search for `purge-old-images` returns zero hits outside
this repository's doc pages. This directory is the record, NOT the source of truth: nothing
deploys from it. `.github/scripts/acr-retention-tasks.sh verify` is what relates the two, and
`… apply` is a maintainer-run command that pushes this record back onto the registry.
Why the record exists at all: the definitions carry the reasoning from two incidents
(Memex#122, MeshWeaver#3438) in comments that live in exactly one place — inside a base64
blob in a cloud resource nobody diffs. A `az acr task update` from any laptop replaces them
silently and completely.
`schedule`/`status`/`timeout` here are ASSERTED by `verify`; the remaining fields are
provenance and are printed, not compared.
The purge was PAUSED from 2026-09-12 (Memex#219) while the protection was incomplete; the
pause was the MITIGATION and MeshWeaver#4081 the FIX. With #4081 closed and the lock lane green
nightly, the pause is lifted and `purge-old-images` is recorded `Enabled` — as a REPORT: both
its steps carry `--dry-run` (see `dryRun`), so it logs what the 30-day window would delete and
deletes nothing. Re-pause by restoring a `pause` block (inForce/since/reason/reEnableWhen) and
recording the task Disabled, then applying.
🚨 A DISABLED TASK STILL SHOWS AN ENABLED TIMER. `az acr task list` reports
`status: Disabled` on the task while its `trigger.timerTriggers[0].status` still reads
`Enabled` at `0 3 * * *`. Read the TASK's status; the trigger's is about the trigger.

tasks.name: purge-old-images
notes: ENABLED as a dry-run report: the pause (2026-09-12, Memex#219) is lifted, `--dry-run` stays on both steps under the top-level `dryRun` block.
ONE task, TWO steps: a 30d step over the CI image repositories, and a separate 30d step
for memex-portal. The filter lists stay SEPARATE even at one window — they are not
symmetric (mw-plugin-test is unique to the first, memex-portal to the second), and a
union-merge would silently retune one of them the next time either window moves.
🚨 The first step was `--ago 7d --keep 10` until 2026-09-13 (MeshWeaver#3438). #3842's
decided rule is at least 30 days by age with NO build-count quota; #3843 and #3846
clamped the bundle store and the assembly cache to it and left the registry out in as
many words. `lock-pinned-digests.py --check-retention-record` now asserts it on every
pull request. APPLIED on 2026-11-02 by the governed `RegistryRetention` apply
(control `Ops/Actions/registry-retention-apply-20261101b-3438`, Memex run 41419066636):
the live task now matches this record byte for byte, still Disabled under `pause`.
Both steps share ONE 3600 s task budget; the per-step `timeout` is a per-step ceiling.
🚨 NEITHER STEP PASSES `--include-locked`, and that is the whole of the pin protection:
`acr purge` skips locked manifests by default. Adding that flag would delete every
manifest `lock-pinned-digests.py` protects.
🚨 THE TAG HALF OF EVERY FILTER IS AN ALLOWLIST OF PER-BUILD IDENTITY SHAPES, anchored
`^…$` because acr-cli SEARCHES the tag regex (`MatchString`) while it anchors the
repository half itself. A tag protected by NAME — a declared release channel, the
`arm-complete-<version>` marker, an official / CD version `x.y.z` — is therefore never
reached, locked or not (MeshWeaver#3438). `--check-retention-record` derives those names
from their readers and reds on any filter that reaches one.

tasks.name: purge-old-ci-releases
notes: SUPERSEDED and DISABLED, not deleted — its filter list was folded into
purge-old-images's two steps. Kept as the record of the Memex#122 reasoning it carries,
and so that re-enabling it is a visible act rather than a rediscovery.
Do not re-enable it: two divergent lists is the defect #3438 named.

recordAheadOfRegistry.what: The record lifts the pause: `purge-old-images` is recorded `Enabled` (the live task is `Disabled`), and its YAML comment no longer says the record is ahead of the registry. The window, the filters and `--dry-run` on both steps are unchanged from what the 2026-11-02 apply installed (control `Ops/Actions/registry-retention-apply-20261101b-3438`, Memex run 41419066636). `purge-old-ci-releases` stays Disabled and unchanged.
recordAheadOfRegistry.why: Lifting the pause is a reviewed diff followed by an approved `RegistryRetention` apply; between the two the record is ahead. `pause.reEnableWhen` was: lock-pinned-digests green on a fleet whose tag references and index closures are locked (MeshWeaver#4081). #4081 is closed, and the lock lane's scheduled runs on main are green (41370289769 on 2026-11-02, 41259318478 on 2026-11-01). The apply's own interlock re-measures that at apply time (newest completed run green and under 36 h old).
recordAheadOfRegistry.clearedBy: the next approved `acr-retention-tasks.sh apply` — after which `verify` finds no drift on `purge-old-images` and reds on THIS declaration being stale; delete it in a core pull request.

dryRun.what: Every `acr purge` step of the listed tasks carries `--dry-run`: the task, once enabled, logs what the decided 30-day window would delete and deletes nothing.
dryRun.why: The window is decided (#3842); what it would select on the live registry is not yet observed. A dry run on the real registry is the only reading of that which does not cost an artifact.
dryRun.liftWhen: At least one nightly run of the enabled task has been read back, and nothing its dry-run output lists is a tag or manifest the fleet references. Then ONE reviewed diff drops `--dry-run` from the steps, deletes this block, and re-declares `recordAheadOfRegistry` until the next approved RegistryRetention apply.
